name: How are unexpected issues and change orders handled during construction?

mainEntity.name: How are unexpected issues and change orders handled during construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unforeseen issues—such as hidden pipe leaks, improper prior wiring, or rotted subfloors—are documented immediately upon discovery during demolition or framing. A responsible general contractor pauses work on the affected section, presents clear photographic evidence to the homeowner, and explains the options and costs before proceeding. Work outside the affected spot often continues so the overall timeline remains active. Change orders are documented in writing so that scope, cost revisions, and any calendar adjustments remain completely transparent before repairs take place.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden issues are documented immediately, presented with practical repair options, and confirmed through written change orders before any extra work begins.
